messages.subject: dplyr::arrange words with accented vowels
parts:
manipulatr-ers,

I think this question is more about Rcpp than dplyr, but dplyr seems to be affected, hence my post here.

In short, why does dplyr::arrange place accented vowels after "z" when alphabetizing words? Specifically, in the following toy example, why does dplyr::arrange incorrectly place the Spanish word "zona" before "órgano", while base::sort correctly places "órgano" before "zona":

> library("dplyr")
> corpus <- data_frame(word = c("zona", "libro", "órgano", "casa"))
> dplyr::arrange(corpus, word)
Source: local data frame [4 x 1]

    word
1   casa
2  libro
3   zona
4 órgano

> sort(corpus$word)
[1] "casa"   "libro"  "órgano" "zona" 
# this is the output I want

Any ideas on how to have dplyr::arrange correctly handle words that begin with accented vowels?

If you're interested, here's my attempt in Rcpp to create a fast table function, sorting the output afterwards. 

Note: I assume there is a way to sort the map directly in the Rcpp function, but I don't have much experience with C++, hence my attempt to use dplyr::arrange to sort the output of the Rcpp function. Any pointers are also appreciated on sorting the map, first on the count (value) in descending order, and then on the word (key) in ascending order, and handling accented vowels correctly.


#include <Rcpp.h>
using namespace Rcpp;

// modified version of tableC in Advanced R: http://adv-r.had.co.nz/Rcpp.html
// [[Rcpp::export]]
std::map<String, int> table_words(CharacterVector x) {
  std::map<String, int> counts;
  int n = x.size();
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    counts[x[i]]++;
  }
  return counts;
}

/*** R
corpus <- c("zona", "libro", "órgano", "casa", "libro")

# Try 1
# using sort() on the output of base::table correctly places "órgano" before "zona"
sort(table(corpus), decreasing = T)

# libro   casa órgano   zona 
# 2      1      1      1 

# Try 2
# sorting the output of an Rcpp version of table (above) incorrectly places "zona" before "órgano", 
sort(table_words(corpus), decreasing = T)

# libro   casa   zona órgano 
# 2      1      1      1 

# Try 3
# using dplyr::arrange to sort the output of an Rcpp version of table (above) also incorrectly places "zona" before "órgano"
temp <- table_words(corpus)
data_frame(word = names(temp), count = temp) %>% arrange(desc(count), word)

# 1  libro     2
# 2   casa     1
# 3   zona     1
# 4 órgano     1

*/
